items.headline: Schedule your most used Copilot prompts
items.summary: Microsoft 365 Copilot now supports scheduled prompts that run recurring questions automatically on a daily, weekly, or monthly cadence and surface results when needed. Instead of manually running the same queries each morning, users can configure Copilot to automatically deliver daily summaries, weekly reports, or monthly analytics directly to their inbox or Teams. Organizations using AI assistants in daily work save an average of two hours per week per employee.

items.headline: Salesforce Launches Agentforce Help Agent That Deploys in Minutes and Only Charges for Resolutions
items.summary: Salesforce launched Agentforce Help Agent with pay-per-resolution pricing at $2 per autonomous resolution, available in general availability July 2026. The agent works across voice, web, portal, and messaging channels and only charges when it resolves an issue autonomously from start to finish. If the customer escalates to a human or leaves unsatisfied, there is no charge. The Help Agent can be set up in 6 clicks or less and is designed to resolve customer issues on day one without extensive configuration.

items.headline: AI Chatbot Cyber Attack 2026: Govt Breach Exposed
items.summary: A campaign beginning in late December 2025 and running for approximately one month compromised around ten Mexican government entities and one financial institution using AI-powered attack tools including Claude Code and ChatGPT. Named targets included Mexico's tax authority, the national electoral institute, city-level systems, and a water utility. Security researchers confirmed the intruder compromised these systems and exfiltrated sensitive records without a human operator directly controlling each step.
items.levelshiftAngle: This incident validates the urgent need for the AI governance frameworks and security controls LevelShift sells as part of Phase 4 (Architecture and Enablement) in our 5-Phase methodology. Use this as a battle card when Financial Services and Healthcare prospects ask why governance costs are justified, and reference it in the next AI Readiness Assessment for any client in critical infrastructure verticals.

items.headline: EU AI Act Transparency Obligations Preparing for Compliance by 2 August 2026
items.summary: Article 50 transparency obligations of the EU AI Act take effect on 2 August 2026, requiring providers of chatbots and generative AI systems to inform users when they are interacting with AI or viewing AI-generated content. Providers must mark AI-generated text, images, audio, and video in a machine-readable format, and deployers must disclose emotion recognition or biometric categorization uses. The AI Omnibus provisional agreement of May 2026 grants generative AI systems already on the market until 2 December 2026 to meet machine-readable marking requirements. Penalties for non-compliance reach up to 35 million euros or 7 percent of worldwide turnover.
